The evolved gases, rich in CO but including combustibles, are sent to the combustor of the gasification unit. The 2 depressurized liquid stream is dehydrated using a molecular sieve system. Downstream of the molecular sieve, the dehydrated alcohol stream is introduced to the crude alcohol distillation column, which separates methanol and ethanol from higher molecular weight alcohols. The overhead stream from the crude alcohol column is separated in a second column to a crude methanol stream and an ethanol product that meets ASTM fuel ethanol specifications. Acid gas 2 removal was modeled using the basis in the 2011 design report where a Selexol system was reported. In many methanation implementations reported in literature Rectisol systems are used instead. However, based on modeling priorities with the resources available, it was decided to maintain the Selexol system for acid gas removal, instead of spending resources on modeling a Rectisol system (Rectisol systems are well documented in literature and can be included separately). Methanation was selected as the final downstream purification step to utilize the remaining syngas and meet the final pipeline specifications for allowable H and CO content. The 2 methanation reactor was modeled as a 3-adiabatic reactor system operating at ~30 bar, with intermediate cooling between reactors.
